title: Focus Toolkit: tools to improve focus and concentration
summary: Huberman models focus as an arrow: epinephrine is the shaft (alertness), acetylcholine the arrowhead (spotlight), dopamine the engine. He lays out mostly zero-cost tools to raise and train focus: sleep, 90-minute bouts, 40 Hz binaural beats, cold exposure, a 13-minute refocusing meditation, NSDR, visual anchoring, caffeine, and select supplements.

principles.text: Focus needs epinephrine (alertness), acetylcholine (spotlight) and dopamine (drive); each tool targets one of these.
principles.quote: these three neurochemicals together, acetylcholine, epinephrine and dopamine really allow you to get focused, to focus very precisely

principles.text: Sleep modulates focus; no tool overcomes chronic sleep deprivation, so get good sleep about 80% of nights.
principles.quote: There is simply no tool that's going to allow you to overcome chronic sleep deprivation and allow you to remain focused, no pill, no device, no supplement, no protocol whatsoever.

principles.text: Work in focus bouts of 90 minutes or less with a 5-10 minute warmup, then deliberately defocus afterward.
principles.quote: the ideal duration is about 90 minutes, not exactly 90 minutes, but we can reliably say 90 minutes or less

principles.text: Use 40 Hz binaural beats for about five minutes before work, or throughout when distractible.
principles.quote: 40 HZ binaural beats have been shown in a number of peer reviewed studies to increase focus and concentration.

principles.text: Deliberate cold exposure for 1-5 minutes raises epinephrine and dopamine and boosts focus for an hour or more.
principles.quote: it should be uncomfortably cold, but safe to stay in for one to five minutes.

principles.text: A daily 13-minute breath meditation that repeatedly refocuses attention trains focus circuits; avoid it within four hours of bedtime.
principles.quote: I recommend that you not do it within the four hours prior to your bedtime.
